---
title: "Will a ranked player stop playing?"
subtitle: "Predicting 28-day churn in League of Legends, honestly"
---

This project predicts whether a ranked League of Legends player will play **no game at all in
the next 28 days**, using only what was knowable at the moment of the prediction. It covers
6,048 players on NA, EUW and KR, from Iron to Diamond, sampled from the ranked ladder through
Riot's API.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
snapshot = FileAttachment("data/snapshot.json").json()
m = snapshot.metrics
pct = (x) => `${(100 * x).toFixed(0)}%`
html`<div class="stat-row">
  <div class="stat"><div class="value">${snapshot.meta.players.toLocaleString()}</div>
    <div class="label">held-out players at ${snapshot.meta.cutoff}</div></div>
  <div class="stat"><div class="value">${pct(snapshot.meta.churn_rate)}</div>
    <div class="label">of them stopped playing</div></div>
  <div class="stat"><div class="value">${m.lightgbm.pr_auc.toFixed(3)}</div>
    <div class="label">PR-AUC of the best model (LightGBM)</div></div>
  <div class="stat"><div class="value">${m.recency.pr_auc.toFixed(3)}</div>
    <div class="label">PR-AUC of "days since the last game" alone</div></div>
</div>`
```

## The honest answer

The best model barely beats the simplest possible rule: **rank players by how long it has been
since their last game**. Every model was tested on players it had never seen, at a later date
than anything it learned from, and the gain over that rule is inside the noise of a test set
with 200 churners.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
labels = ({majority: "Majority class", recency: "Recency rule (days since the last game)",
  logreg: "Logistic regression", lightgbm: "LightGBM", mlp: "MLP",
  gru: "GRU over the last 20 matches", lightgbm_gru: "LightGBM + GRU average"})
html`<table class="table table-sm">
  <thead><tr><th>Model</th><th>PR-AUC</th><th>ROC-AUC</th><th>Brier</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>${Object.entries(m).map(([k, r]) => html`<tr>
    <td>${labels[k] ?? k}</td><td>${r.pr_auc.toFixed(3)}</td>
    <td>${r.roc_auc.toFixed(3)}</td><td>${r.brier.toFixed(3)}</td></tr>`)}</tbody>
</table>`
```

<p class="small-note">PR-AUC rewards finding the players who stop; a random guess scores the
churn rate. Lower Brier is better. Intervals and comparisons are on the
<a href="model-card.qmd">model card</a>.</p>

## Why it's hard

Most players who stop had already been away for a while: 69% of them hadn't played for a week
or more at the cutoff. Among players on a break, nothing in their history tells a break from
quitting much better than the length of the break itself. Win rate, KDA and other in-game
statistics carry almost no signal. That is a finding, not a failure: it says where the signal
isn't.

## The first version, and its leak

The 2024 version of this project reported 91% accuracy. Its features leaked the label: matches
were bucketed by date across all players, so a player who had quit was the one with an empty
"late" bucket, and the model learned the answer. This version builds every feature from data
before the prediction date only, and a test deletes everything after that date and checks that
no feature changes.

## What's next: a forward test

On 2026-10-25, the models predicted for 3,718 players whether they would play between
2026-10-22 and 2026-11-19. The predictions were frozen and their fingerprint (SHA-256) was
committed to the repository before any of those weeks was collected, so they can't be adjusted
after the fact. They are scored after 2026-11-19, on outcomes nobody had seen.
